newsitem.title: INDIA: India gold ends up but off day's high, silver down.
newsitem.headline: India gold ends up but off day's high, silver down.

text.p: ** Indian gold 24 carat ends Wednesday 5 rupees higher at 4,735 rupees. Gold opened 20 rupees higher at 4,750 rupees but failed to consolidate gains amid sluggish seasonal buying.
** Gold biscuits (116.50 gramme each) close 100 rupees higher at 55,400 rupees.
** Silver (.999) closes 25 rupees lower at 7,280 rupees per kg on fresh arrivals of imported silver. Industrial buyers keep to sidelines in a falling market.

Gold 24 carat closed five rupees higher from Tuesday's close of 4,730 rupees but off the intra-day high of 4,750 rupees, dealers said. They said gold opened higher on overnight gains in the world market but sluggish seasonal demand led to profit-taking which eroded the early gains.
Gold was down by 40 rupees per 10 gramme on Tuesday.
Prices of gold biscuits closed at 55,400 rupees after opening higher at 55,500 rupees, dealers said. They closed Tuesday at 55,300 rupees.

Silver (.999) closed 25 rupees lower at 7,280 rupees per kg on continued arrivals of the imported metal while a weak trend in the world market prompted fresh unloading by stockists, dealers said. Silver was down 50 rupees per kg on Tuesday.
Dealers said industrial buyers kept to the sidelines expecting further price erosion and sentiments were subdued at close. (Conversion $1=35.89 rupees)
